rationale: The Old English verb a-teáh (past tense of a-tēon) carries the core sense of pulling or dragging something physically, as attested in Beowulf (B. 766) where it describes physical force (Grendel drawing/pulling away). This aligns best with pull.v.01 "cause to move by pulling," the most concrete and literal pulling sense, rather than secondary senses like extracting from a container or moving gradually.
